session_capability_disclosure.detail: This idea-generator session was launched WITHOUT any shell/execution tool (available tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, WebSearch, WebFetch, SendMessage). No PARI/GP, cypari, Sage, or Python could be run. Therefore NOTHING in this file was certified by computation.
session_capability_disclosure.what_verified_here_means: Exactly three things: (i) bibliographic retrieval of a primary or corroborating source over the network, with the identifier recorded; (ii) hand algebra that a reader can redo on paper -- degree bookkeeping for the Shioda-Tate degree d, and leading-coefficient consistency checks between a transcribed equation and a transcribed point; (iii) agreement between two independently-prompted extractions of the same source text. Everything else is CITED.
what_could_not_be_done_here: verifying that any published section satisfies its Weierstrass equation as a polynomial identity in t
computing any Mordell-Weil rank, regulator, minimal model, or naive height
OCR of scanned Project Euclid PDFs (no poppler/pdftoppm in the environment; the Read tool refused PDF rendering)

conventions.shioda_tate_ceiling: For an elliptic surface with section over an algebraically closed field, of arithmetic degree d (chi(O_S) = d, Euler number 12d, h^{1,1} = 10d): rank MW <= rho - 2 - sum_v (m_v - 1) <= 10d - 2. d=1 (rational elliptic surface) -> 8; d=2 (K3) -> 18; d=3 -> 28; d=4 -> 38.
conventions.elkies_k3_over_Q_refinement: For elliptic K3 surfaces the geometric ceiling 18 is not attainable with all sections rational over Q(T); the attainable maximum over Q(T) is 17. Cited from arXiv:0709.2908 (see family ELKIES-K3-17). This program did not re-derive that argument.
conventions.rank_field_discipline: Every rank below is reported separately over Q(t) and over Q-bar(t). Where a source states only one of the two, the other is recorded as 'unknown' and NOT inferred, except for the trivial inequality rank_{Q(t)} <= rank_{Q-bar(t)}.
conventions.d_lower_bound_rule: From any geometric rank r one gets 10d - 2 >= r, i.e. d >= ceil((r+2)/10). This is used below as an UNCONDITIONAL derivation that does not depend on any transcribed equation.

families.name: Mestre's rank >= 11 (and >= 12) construction over Q(T)
families.status: RECOMMENDED BASE -- reproducible in this repo from a published recipe; coefficients NOT computed here

primary_citation.ref: J.-F. Mestre, 'Courbes elliptiques de rang >= 11 sur Q(T)', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I Math. 313 (1991), 139-142
primary_citation.companion: J.-F. Mestre, 'Courbes elliptiques de rang >= 12 sur Q(T)', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I Math. 313 (1991), 171-174
primary_citation.provenance: retrieved (bibliographic data only; the CRAS notes themselves were NOT opened in this session -- no accessible full text found)
primary_citation.verified_by: web search returning consistent volume/page data; corroborated by the reference list of arXiv:math/0406579

corroborating_citation.ref: arXiv:math/0406579, S. Arms, A. Lozano-Robledo, S. J. Miller, 'Constructing Elliptic Curves over Q(T) with Moderate Rank', Section 1 (Introduction)
corroborating_citation.provenance: retrieved (HTML full text read via https://arxiv.org/html/math/0406579v1)
corroborating_citation.claim_relied_on: This paper states Mestre's construction step by step and prints two working 6-tuples.

construction.step_1: q(x) = prod_{i=1}^{6} (x - a_i), for a 6-tuple of integers a_i
construction.step_2: p(x,T) = q(x - T) q(x + T)   [degree 12 in x]
construction.step_3: there exist g(x,T) of degree 6 in x and r(x,T) of degree at most 5 in x with p(x,T) = g(x,T)^2 - r(x,T)
construction.step_4: the curve is  y^2 = r(x,T)  over Q(T)
construction.step_5: when r has degree 3 or 4 in x the 12 points P_{+-i}(T) = (+-T + a_i, g(+-T + a_i)) lie on it
construction.why_the_sections_are_free: p(+-T + a_i, T) = 0 by construction, so g(+-T+a_i)^2 = r(+-T+a_i, T) IDENTICALLY in T. The section-on-curve check is therefore an immediate consequence of the single polynomial identity p = g^2 - r, and needs no point search. This is the property that makes the family cheap to re-certify here.

weierstrass_coefficients_in_t.status: NOT COMPUTED IN THIS SESSION (no CAS available). The recipe above determines them exactly and deterministically from the 6-tuple; the executor can produce them in seconds.
weierstrass_coefficients_in_t.predicted_T_degrees: By the weighted-degree argument (assign weight 1 to both x and T; p is weighted-homogeneous of top weight 12 and the weight-12 and weight-11 parts of g^2 cancel it), deg_T r_k <= 10 - k, i.e. (r_4, r_3, r_2, r_1, r_0) have T-degree at most (6, 7, 8, 9, 10). DERIVED HERE by hand, NOT taken from a source; must be confirmed by the executor's actual computation.

rank_over_Qt.source: Mestre's own titles, which state the field as Q(T)

rank_over_Qbart.qualifier: at_least (trivial consequence of the Q(T) claim)
rank_over_Qbart.verified_here: only the inequality rank_{Q(t)} <= rank_{Q-bar(t)}, which is definitional

surface_degree_d.derivation: UNCONDITIONAL: rank 11 over Q-bar(T) forces 10d - 2 >= 11, so d >= 1.3, so d >= 2. Exact d NOT determined here.
surface_degree_d.upper_bound_estimate: If the predicted T-degrees (6,7,8,9,10) are right, the quartic invariants I = 12 r_4 r_0 - 3 r_3 r_1 + r_2^2 and J = 72 r_4 r_2 r_0 + 9 r_3 r_2 r_1 - 27 r_4 r_1^2 - 27 r_0 r_3^2 - 2 r_2^3 have T-degree at most 16 and 24, giving a Weierstrass model Y^2 = X^3 - 27 I X - 27 J with deg A <= 16, deg B <= 24, hence d <= 4 before minimalisation. DERIVED HERE by hand; cancellation may reduce it. The executor must compute the minimal model and read off d.

generators_published.form: the 12 points P_{+-i}(T) = (+-T + a_i, g(+-T + a_i)) on the quartic model
generators_published.note: 12 points on a genus-1 quartic model give rank >= 11 only after the relations are accounted for; Mestre's claim is >= 11. This program must re-certify independence, not inherit it.

internal_consistency_check_run_here.method: Substitute x = (t+703)/15 into the transcribed quartic, multiply through by 15^4 = 50625, and compare with 9*N(t)^2 where N(t) = -224t^3 - 844t^2 + 900484t + 2161725. Both sides are degree 6; compare the t^6 and t^5 coefficients. This is pure hand arithmetic and needs no computer.
internal_consistency_check_run_here.verdict: FAILS. The transcribed point does not lie on the transcribed curve.
internal_consistency_check_run_here.interpretation: At least one of the two transcriptions is corrupted, or they refer to different models/parameters (Scholten's abstract uses z as the function-field variable, so a variable mismatch is plausible). This is a statement about THIS SESSION'S retrieval pipeline, NOT a claim that the published paper is wrong.
internal_consistency_check_run_here.secondary_observation: The transcribed quartic contains only EVEN powers of t, while the transcribed point contains odd powers. A curve defined over Q(t^2) would be a quadratic base change, and its sections would split into eigenspaces under t -> -t, so this is not by itself contradictory -- but combined with the failed coefficient check it is a second reason to distrust the transcription (an extractor dropping odd-power terms would produce exactly this pattern).

RED_FLAG_source_discrepancy.statement: Nagao's own paper is TITLED 'An example of elliptic curve over Q(T) with rank >= 13'. Scholten proves the rank over Q(t) is exactly 12 and the rank over Q-bar(t) is exactly 13. Read literally the title claims >= 13 over Q(T), which Scholten's Corollary 1 contradicts.
RED_FLAG_source_discrepancy.resolution_status: UNRESOLVED HERE. The Nagao full text was not readable in this session, so it is not known whether Nagao's own statement is over Q(T) or over Q-bar(T), or whether one of the 13 points is only defined over a quadratic extension.
RED_FLAG_source_discrepancy.consequence_for_this_campaign: Use 12, not 13, as the Q(t) base rank for Nagao. The coordinator's handoff already states this; this task confirms the 12/13 split from a retrievable peer source and adds the observation that the primary title disagrees with it.
RED_FLAG_source_discrepancy.do_not: Do not average, and do not silently adopt 13.

surface_degree_d.derivation_lower: UNCONDITIONAL: geometric rank 13 forces 10d - 2 >= 13, so d >= 1.5, so d >= 2. Hence Nagao's surface is NOT a rational elliptic surface and its rank is not capped at 8.
surface_degree_d.derivation_upper: CONDITIONAL on the transcription: with x-degree-4 coefficients of t-degrees (2,2,4,4,6), the quartic invariants I and J have t-degree at most 8 and 12, so the Weierstrass model has deg A <= 8, deg B <= 12, i.e. d <= 2. families.name: Quadratic base change of this program's own rank-8 rational elliptic surface (GOAL-ECQ-001)
families.status: PROGRAM-INTERNAL PROPOSAL, NOT A RETRIEVED FAMILY -- speculative, listed so the campaign has a route that carries zero retrieval risk
families.novelty_status: adaptation (the eigenspace decomposition of a quadratic base change is standard; no source was checked for this exact use, so treat as unverified)
families.construction: Let E : y^2 = x^3 + A(t) x + B(t) be the rank-8 rational elliptic surface already built in GOAL-ECQ-001 (deg A <= 4, deg B <= 6, d = 1, ceiling 8). Substitute t = s^2. The surface E' : y^2 = x^3 + A(s^2) x + B(s^2) has deg A' <= 8, deg B' <= 12, hence d = 2 (K3) and ceiling 18. The involution s -> -s splits MW(E'/Q(s)) into its invariant part, which is MW(E/Q(t)) of rank 8, and its anti-invariant part, which is MW of the quadratic twist E^{(t)}/Q(t).
families.predicted_rank_over_Qt: 8 + rank_{Q(t)} E^{(t)}. Breaking the cap requires only that the twist have a single non-torsion section.
why_it_is_attractive: the 8 invariant sections are already in hand and already certified in this repo, so 8 of the 9 needed independent sections cost nothing
coefficients stay exactly as small as the existing rank-8 family's, which is the ONLY candidate property that keeps the ICARM naive height low

the anti-invariant sections are automatically independent of the invariant ones -- they live in different eigenspaces of the s -> -s action, which is the same purely algebraic independence certificate already used in experiments/EXP-ECRANK-e1e30e/source/twist_family.py
families.why_it_may_fail: rank_{Q(t)} E^{(t)} may be 0, in which case the base change buys nothing and the family has rank exactly 8 over Q(s) with the cap merely relocated from d=1 to d=2. That is a real negative outcome and it is cheap to observe.
verified_here: the degree bookkeeping giving d = 2 and ceiling 18
the eigenspace independence argument, which is algebraic

height_feasibility_note_for_H_ECQ_d60d07.why_this_matters: The hypothesis needs rank >= 15 at naive height < 118.770. Calibration from the pre-registered frontier: the rank-30 curve has ~63-digit coefficients and naive height 442.085, consistent with naive height ~ log(max(|a4|^3, |a6|^2)). Height 118.770 then corresponds to |a4| ~ e^39.6 ~ 1.6e17 (18 digits) or |a6| ~ 6e25.
height_feasibility_note_for_H_ECQ_d60d07.consequence: A base family whose OWN coefficients already exceed ~1e17 cannot produce a curve under that height at ANY specialisation, small t or not, unless minimalisation removes a large 12th-power factor. Nagao's transcribed quartic has coefficients up to 6.5e18 before passing to Weierstrass form, where -27*I and -27*J push them to ~1e37; the naive height of a generic specialisation would be ~250, more than double the target.
height_feasibility_note_for_H_ECQ_d60d07.the_countervailing_fact: Those coefficients carry visible content: 14017536 = 2^10 * 3^4 * 13^2, and 330112972800 = 14017536 * 23550 exactly. A large common factor can be partly removed by minimalisation, so the estimate above is an upper bound on the height, not a verdict.
height_feasibility_note_for_H_ECQ_d60d07.status: THIS IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Nothing was computed. It is written down because it is the cheapest thing that could falsify the campaign's height premise and it should be measured FIRST.
